newsitem.title: USA: Interstate, Host Marriott buy Radisson hotel.
newsitem.headline: Interstate, Host Marriott buy Radisson hotel.

text.p: Host Marriott Corp. and Interstate Hotels Co. bought the Manhattan Beach Radisson Plaza hotel in Manhattan Beach, Calif., for $38.25 million, the companies said Monday.
Marriott will have a 75 percent interest in the full-service hotel three miles from Los Angeles, while Interstate will have 25 percent, the companies said.
The 380-room hotel will be converted to a Marriott and will be managed by Pittsburgh-based Interstate, the companies said.
Host Marriott Chief Operating Officer Christopher Nassetta predicted a strong improvement in operating results once the property is converted to a Marriott.
About $6.8 million in capital expenditures have been allocated to convert the property, Interstate said.
The hotel features a nine-hole golf course, about 21,000 square feet of meeting space, two restaurants, a health club, lobby bar, lounge and a four-level parking garage.

Host Marriott owns or holds controlling interests in 87 hotels operating mainly under the Marriott and Ritz-Carlton names. It also serves as general partner and has minority interests in partnerships that own 250 lodgings, including 30 full-service hotels.
Interstate owns, manages, leases or performs related services for 229 hotels. It owns or has a controlling interest in 33 properties.
Radisson Hospitality Worldwide, with headquarters in Minneapolis, is part of privately owned Carlson Companies Inc.
Host Marriott stock rose 12.5 cents to $19.50 and Interstate dipped 12.5 cents to $27.125, both in consolidated morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
